Ollama.d: A free tool that downloads open-weight models and runs them on your own computer, with a simple command line and a local HTTP API on port 11434.

llama.cpp.d: An open-source C/C++ engine for running language models efficiently on laptops, workstations and servers, using CPUs or GPUs. It reads models in the GGUF format.

GGUF.d: The single-file model format used by llama.cpp. It holds the (usually quantised) weights plus the tokenizer, model settings and chat template needed to run them.

Modelfile.d: A small text file used by Ollama to build a named variant of a model with a fixed system prompt and settings such as temperature and context length.

Data parallelism.d: Splitting training across chips by giving each chip a copy of the model and different training examples, then averaging their gradients after every step.

Pipeline parallelism.d: Splitting a model across chips by layers, so each chip handles one stage and passes its results to the next, like an assembly line.

Tensor parallelism.d: Splitting each layer's large matrices across several chips that compute their parts at the same time and combine the results. It needs very fast links between chips.

Mixed-precision training.d: Training with fast 16-bit (or lower) numbers for most calculations while keeping a 32-bit master copy of the weights so small updates aren't lost.

Compute-optimal training.d: Choosing model size and amount of training data to get the best model for a fixed training compute budget. The 2022 Chinchilla paper found both should grow together, often summarised as about 20 tokens per parameter.

Continuous batching.d: A serving technique that re-forms the batch at every decoding step, so finished requests leave and waiting ones join immediately, keeping the GPU busy.

PagedAttention.d: A method, introduced with vLLM in 2023, that stores each request's KV cache in small fixed-size pages allocated on demand, nearly eliminating wasted memory.

Prefix caching.d: Reusing the stored KV cache for text that many requests start with, such as a long system prompt, so it doesn't have to be processed again. The server-side idea behind prompt caching.

Speculative decoding.d: Speeding up text generation by letting a small model draft several tokens that the large model then checks in one pass, keeping the large model's output unchanged.

vLLM.d: A widely used open-source engine for serving language models at high throughput, known for PagedAttention and continuous batching, with an OpenAI-compatible API.
